URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/23/why-a-north-sea-oilfield-is-emerging-as-british-pm-burnhams-big-test
(WebFetch — Al Jazeera, 23 July 2026)

Rosebank is the UK's largest unexploited oil and gas field, ~130km from Shetland. In 2023 Norwegian company Equinor received permission to drill. A January 2025 court ruling determined that consent for both Rosebank and Shell's Jackdaw field "had been granted unlawfully," requiring new government approval with downstream emissions now factored into assessments.

Burnham's position: "Burnham and his team have not commented" on reports he might support North Sea drilling. The final decision rests with Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh following a public notice period closing 17 August.

Trump: Reports of potential approval "have led to celebrations from United States President Donald Trump, a longtime advocate of fossil fuel projects."

Robert Palmer (Uplift): "Rosebank is the key climate test for this government. The science is really clear that going ahead with Rosebank is just not compatible with the UK's climate commitments."

Financial stakes: Ithaca Energy holds a 20% stake in Rosebank.
